answer: I would like to talk about someone who has made me laugh more than anyone else I know. The funniest person I know is an old school friend who has an incredible talent for making people laugh. We sat next to each other for most of secondary school, and we still meet up whenever he is back in Sirajganj, usually at our old favourite tea stall. What makes him special is that his humour is completely [[spontaneous]]; he does not tell rehearsed jokes but reacts to whatever is happening in the moment. I remember one particularly dull afternoon during our final exams when the stress was unbearable, and within minutes he had the whole group in stitches. He did a perfect impression of a nervous exam invigilator, complete with a dramatic search for a missing pencil. His timing is [[impeccable]], and he has a gift for finding the funny side of even the most awkward situations. What I appreciate most is that his jokes are never [[malicious]]; he laughs with people, not at them. As for how I felt, I laughed so much that my stomach hurt, and for the first time in weeks I completely forgot about the exams. Honestly, he has lifted my mood on countless bad days, which is a genuine gift. I think people who can make others laugh so easily are quietly valuable, because laughter is such good medicine. Being around him is always [[uplifting]], and I feel lucky to count him as a friend.

followUps.q: Do you think you have a good sense of humour?
followUps.answer: I think so, although mine is drier and quieter than his. I enjoy [[wordplay]] and gentle teasing more than big jokes, and my family says I am funniest when I do not mean to be.

followUps.q: Is laughter important in your life?
followUps.answer: Very much. After a stressful day at work, a good laugh with my family over dinner helps me unwind more than anything else. I think it keeps us close as well.

note: Added how I know him, what exactly he did during the exams and how I felt at the time, keeping the humour kind.
